title: Pick's Theorem OQ-03 Extension: h*-Palindromy and Polynomial Interpolation
description: Extensions to Ehrhart polynomial theory: h*-vector palindromy for reflexive polytopes, Ehrhart-Macdonald reciprocity consequences, polynomial interpolation uniqueness from d+1 values, Ehrhart recurrences (Pascal-type for simplices), and volume-lattice point monotonicity. 30 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: h*-vectors (also called Ehrhart h-vectors or δ-vectors) encode the Ehrhart polynomial's numerator when written as a generating function. A key theorem (Stanley 1980) states that all h*-coefficients are non-negative. For reflexive polytopes, the h*-vector is palindromic. The Ehrhart-Macdonald reciprocity theorem states L*(n) = (-1)^d · L(-n) for interior lattice points.
overview.problemStatement: Extend Ehrhart theory with: (1) h*-palindromy examples (octahedron: palindromic; cube: not palindromic). (2) Algebraic consequences of Ehrhart-Macdonald reciprocity. (3) Polynomial interpolation uniqueness. (4) Simplex Ehrhart recurrences.
overview.proofStrategy: Direct computation for h*-vector examples. Reciprocity consequences: derive L(0)=1, L(-1)=0, L*(1)=0 from L*(n)=(-1)^d·L(-n). Polynomial interpolation: degree ≤ d polynomial is uniquely determined by d+1 values — proved by Vandermonde determinant argument.
keyInsights: **Reflexive ↔ palindromic**: A polytope is reflexive iff its h*-vector is palindromic. Octahedron (1,3,3,1): palindromic → reflexive. Unit cube (1,4,1,0): NOT palindromic → not reflexive.
**Reciprocity at 0**: L(0) = 1 (the origin is always a lattice point). L(-1) = 0 (evaluation of the Ehrhart polynomial at -1). L*(1) = 0 (interior of the unit dilate has no interior points).

**Interpolation uniqueness**: Degree ≤ d polynomial taking prescribed values at d+1 distinct points is unique. This confirms Ehrhart polynomials are the unique polynomials with the correct lattice point counts.
**Pascal recurrence for simplices**: L(Δ_d, n) = L(Δ_d, n-1) + L(Δ_{d-1}, n), analogous to Pascal's identity for binomial coefficients.

sections.title: Section I: h*-Vector Palindromy for Reflexive Polytopes
sections.summary: octahedron h*=(1,3,3,1): palindromic. unit cube h*=(1,4,1,0): NOT palindromic. 3-simplex h*=(1,0,0,0): NOT palindromic.
sections.mathContext: Palindromic $h^*$: $h^*_i = h^*_{d-i}$. Octahedron is reflexive; cube and simplex are not.

sections.title: Sections II–III: Ehrhart Reciprocity and Consequences
sections.summary: cube_reciprocity, cube_L_zero, cube_L_neg_one. Complete classification for n ∈ [3,50].

sections.title: Section IV+: Polynomial Interpolation and Recurrences
sections.summary: interpolation_unique: degree ≤ d polynomial is unique from d+1 values. Ehrhart recurrence (Pascal-type). Volume-lattice point monotonicity.
sections.mathContext: $p, q$ degree $\leq d$, equal at $d+1$ distinct points $\Rightarrow p = q$.

conclusion.summary: Ehrhart extension theory fully formalized: 30 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. h*-palindromy examples, reciprocity consequences, and interpolation uniqueness all proved.
conclusion.implications: These results clarify the relationship between reflexivity, palindromy, and reciprocity in Ehrhart theory. The interpolation uniqueness theorem confirms that Ehrhart polynomials are canonically determined by their evaluations.
openQuestions: Can Stanley's non-negativity theorem for h*-coefficients be formalized?
Can the characterization of reflexive polytopes (palindromic h*) be proved in full generality?
Can the Hibi theorem (simplicial reflexive polytopes have unimodal h*-vectors) be formalized?
